info.bio:
Inicialmente, Adam Ant, se basó en el uso intenso de la guitarra propio del post punk, más tarde pasó al pop y luego retornó como un cantante para el público adulto. Sus grabaciones más que influyentes eran una muestra de los movimientos en los que se inscribió.

 Adam Ant (Stuart Leslie Goddard), nació en Londres el 3 de noviembre de1954. Hijo único de una familia de trabajadores, tuvo las oportunidades básicas de estudio de un chico de su generación.

scenes.name: Adam and the Ants
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Estudiante de arte punk y artista de culto fetichista («Whip in My Valise», «Zerox», Jubilee de Derek Jarman), Adam paga a McLaren para que le reinvente y es despedido de su propia banda. Se venga usando mejor las ideas de su ex mentor: imagen heroica mitad pirata mitad apache, dos baterías burundesas y la guitarra a lo Duane Eddy y Morricone de Marco Pirroni. Kings of the Wild Frontier (1980), «Stand and Deliver» y «Prince Charming» (1981), un vals de grito de guerra. Bubblegum pop sin drogas ni rebeldía rockera que acaba en el Royal Variety Show: «artista de culto es un eufemismo de perdedor».

xref.title: First Live Gig (November 6, 1975)
xref.body: The band's first live gig took place in London at an art school called St. Martin's. It was held in a small upstairs room with only a dozen people in attendance, who were primarily there to see the headliners, Bizzouca Joe, featuring Adam Ant. The Sex Pistols' performance was cut short after only two songs when the school's social programmer pulled the plug. Despite the brevity and lack of immediate success, this event marked a significant turning point in music history. "And despite the fact that their first live gig wasn't much of a hit, music was never to be quite the same."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Headliner at Sex Pistols' First Gig (November 6, 1975)
xref.body: Vasuka Jo, featuring singer Adam Ant, was the headlining act at St. Martin's art school in London on November 6, 1975, when the Sex Pistols played their notoriously short first live gig as an opening act. "They were all there to see the headliners, group called Vasuka Jo that featured a singer by the name of Adam Ant."

xref.title: Bipolar Disorder
xref.body: A significant factor in Scott Weiland's and Mary Forsberg's struggles was their undiagnosed bipolar disorder, which led to extreme mood swings and poor judgment, often exacerbated by self-medication with drugs like crack. Doctors initially misdiagnosed him with severe depression, and the treatments did not control his manic episodes. "A big part of their problems coping with life is that they were both undiagnosed sufferers of bipolar disorder, and this is a really important part of our story."
